items.title: Step 1
items.description:
In this workshop, you'll learn how to work with conditional statements and comparison operators.

Begin by declaring a variable named `truthyOrFalsy` and assign it the boolean value `true`.

hints.text: You should have a variable named `truthyOrFalsy`.
You should assign `true` to your `truthyOrFalsy` variable.

items.title: Step 2
items.description:
As you learned in a previous lesson, booleans are a data type with only `true` and `false` values.

A truthy value is a value that evaluates to `true` in a boolean context. Examples of truthy values are:

- Non-empty strings
- Non-zero numbers
- The boolean `true`

And other values you'll meet later on.

You can use the `Boolean()` function to check the truthiness of a value. For example, `Boolean("Hello World!")` will return `true` because `"Hello World!"` is truthy.

Now, call `Boolean(truthyOrFalsy)` and log the result to the console.

hints.text: You should log `Boolean(truthyOrFalsy)` to the console.

items.title: Step 3
items.description: Change the assignment of `truthyOrFalsy` by setting its value to `"freeCodeCamp"`. You will still see `true` logged to the console because a non-empty string is a truthy value.

hints.text: Your `truthyOrFalsy` variable should have the value `"freeCodeCamp"`.

items.title: Step 4
items.description:
Falsy values are values that evaluate to `false` in a boolean context. Examples of falsy values are:

- `""` (empty string)
- `0`
- `false`
- `null`
- `undefined`
- `NaN`

You'll meet all of these going through this coursework.

For now, change the assignment of `truthyOrFalsy` by setting its value to an empty string. After that, you'll see `false` logged to the console.

hints.text: You should assign an empty string to `truthyOrFalsy`.

items.title: Step 5
items.description: Now that you know what truthy and falsy values are, remove both your variable declaration and `console.log` statement from your code.

hints.text: You should not have a `truthyOrFalsy` variable.
You should not have `console.log(Boolean(truthyOrFalsy))` in your code.

items.title: Step 6
items.description: Declare a variable named `hasDeveloperJob` and assign it the boolean value `true`.

hints.text: You should have a variable named `hasDeveloperJob`.
You should assign `true` to your `hasDeveloperJob` variable.

items.title: Step 7

hints.text: You should have an `if` statement.
Your `if` statement should use `hasDeveloperJob` as its condition.
You should log `"Timmy is employed as a developer."` to the console within your `if` statement.

items.title: Step 8
items.description: Declare another variable named `isTimmyAGamer` and assign it the boolean `false`.

hints.text: You should declare a variable named `isTimmyAGamer`.
You should assign the boolean value `false` to your `isTimmyAGamer` variable.

items.title: Step 9
items.description:
Now create another `if` statement that uses `isTimmyAGamer` as its condition. Inside the body of your `if` statement, log `"Timmy loves to play World of Warcraft."` to the console.

Note that you won't see anything logged to the console as the condition of your new `if` statement is false.

hints.text: You should have two `if` statements in your code.
Your second `if` statement should use `isTimmyAGamer` as its condition.
You should log `"Timmy loves to play World of Warcraft."` to the console within your second `if` statement.
hints.test: assert.match(__helpers.removeJSComments(code), /(?:\bif\s*\(.+\)\s*\{.+\}.*)\bif\s*\(\s*isTimmyAGamer\s*\)\s*\{\s*console\s*\.\s*log\s*\(\s*('|"|`)Timmy loves to play World of Warcraft.\1\s*\)\s*;?\s*\}/s);

items.title: Step 10
items.description: Declare another variable named `timmyAge` and set it to `18`.

hints.text: You should have a variable named `timmyAge`.
You should assign `18` to your `timmyAge` variable.

items.title: Step 11

hints.text: You should have a third `if` statement in your code.
Your third `if` statement should use `timmyAge >= 16` as its condition.
You should log `"Timmy is old enough to drive."` to the console inside your third `if` statement.

items.title: Step 12

hints.text: Your third `if` statement should have an `else` clause.
You should log `"Timmy is not old enough to drive."` to the console within the body of your `else` clause.
hints.test: assert.match(__helpers.removeJSComments(code), /const\s+timmyAge\s*\=\s*.+\bif\s*\(\s*timmyAge\s*>=\s*16\s*\)\s*\{\s*console\s*\.\s*log\s*\(\s*('|"|`)Timmy is old enough to drive.\1\s*\)\s*;?\s*\}\s*else\s*\{\s*console\s*\.\s*log\s*\(\s*('|"|`)Timmy is not old enough to drive.\2\s*\)\s*;?\s*\}/s);

items.title: Step 13
items.description: Finally, change the declaration of `timmyAge` and set it to a number less than `16`. After that you'll see `"Timmy is not old enough to drive."` logged to the console.

hints.text: Your `timmyAge` variable should have a value less than `16`.
